text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- France posts record trade surplus for 1996 at 122.3 billion francs.

-- Renault SA carmaker's 1996 operating losses are expected to reach some 2 to 2.5 billion francs, total net loss including restructuring provisions may reach four to five billion francs, according to a corporate source.
-- Total SA oil group considers selling U.S. based refineries and petrol stations.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Five banking-sector unions ready to negotiate reform of a 1937 decree setting working hours, but ask for compensation considered unrealistic by banks.
-- Sluggish domestic demand partly accounts for record trade surplus registered in 1996.
-- Cie de Navigation Mixte considers a share buyback, shares are suspended. U.S. investment fund Wyser Pratte and Verneuil Finance see a price of 1,231 francs per share.
L'AGEFI
-- Cie Financiere de Paribas may be forced to launch a buyout offer on subsidiary Navigation Mixte.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Valeo SA auto parts maker posts record 1996 profit at 1.2 billion francs, up 18.8 percent from previous year.
-- Credit Lyonnais managing director Michel Renault to become head of supervisory board at DMC.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- France's share in global trade has decreased last year despite a record trade surplus.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Low demand helps France post record trade surplus.
-- Sanofi 1996 profit rose 19 percent to 1.74 billion francs, as its beauty products unit returned to profit.
